core_rule: Plan and deliver presentations. Use voice (tone, volume, pitch, pace) and multimodal tools. Goal: engage audience.

hint_levels.template: How voice changes keep audience focus?
Presentation like movie trailer. Need right music, images, voice to sell story.

worked_example.question: You are presenting a speech about saving the Great Barrier Reef. How should you change your voice when describing the beauty of the coral versus the threat of bleaching?
worked_example.answer: Use a bright, enthusiastic tone for beauty; shift to a lower, serious tone for threats.

steps.instruction: Identify the different moods or sections within your speech script.
Select voice features like pitch and pace that match the positive section.
steps.result: Higher pitch and faster pace to show excitement.

steps.instruction: Select voice features that match the negative or serious section.
steps.result: Lower pitch and slower pace to show gravity.

worked_example.explanation: Tone matches mood. Serious topic needs low pitch. Exciting topic needs high pitch.

learning_objectives: Identify voice features: pitch, pace, volume, tone
Create multimodal presentations using images and sound

explanation_sections.heading: What is Multimodal Presentation?
explanation_sections.body: Multimodal presentations mix words, images, sound. Goal: grab audience attention. Use speech for story. Use visuals for proof.

explanation_sections.heading: How to Plan and Deliver
explanation_sections.body: Plan structure first. Select visuals to support ideas. Rehearse voice. High pitch shows excitement. Low pitch shows serious facts. Fast pace builds energy. Slow pace adds drama.

explanation_sections.heading: Model Text Example
explanation_sections.body: "Imagine a world without colour." (Spoken slowly with a low, somber tone to create impact). Visual: Black and white photo of a dead reef.

explanation_sections.heading: Common Pitfall: Reading Slides
explanation_sections.body: Reading from slides. Audience stops listening. Use slides for images or short cues. Use voice to tell story.

key_vocabulary.definition: How high or low a sound is.
Using many ways to communicate, like text, image, and sound.

common_mistakes: Speaking too fast due to nerves.
real_world_connections: YouTubers use pace to keep viewers.
News anchors use tone for serious stories.
Game streamers use pitch for excitement.

additional_worked_examples.question: A student slide has 200 words of text. How to fix for a presentation?
additional_worked_examples.answer: Reduce text to three bullet points. Add one high-quality image.

steps.instruction: Identify the core message of the 200-word block.
Replace long sentences with short, punchy keywords.
